messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: inference-runtime (us-east-1) — GPU queue depth spiked to ~1,280 and remains high, autoscaler unable to provision compatible capacity. severity=P2

miguel (oncall): acked and taking initial triage. looping in eng-sre and eng-runtime: @ben @alice please standby.

miguel (oncall): early impact: intermittent 504s on streaming endpoints, increased client retries, and elevated request timeouts. CS notified.

alice (eng-runtime): digging into scheduler logs — lots of placement rejects referencing MIG fragmentation. Looks like lots of small leftover slices across nodes.

alice (eng-runtime): scheduler excerpts:
```
E scheduler/placement.go:142: cannot schedule pod: contiguous GPU slice not found, required=2g, available fragments=[0.5g,0.75g,1g]
E runtime/alloc.go:220: attempted allocation failed for profile=mig-1g-1, node=gpu-node-11, reason=fragmented-slices
```

ben (eng-sre): running quick node inventory to confirm.
ben (eng-sre): `kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,alloc:.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu`
ben (eng-sre): sample output:
```
gpu-node-11 3x1g + 0.5g (fragmented)
gpu-node-12 4x1g
gpu-node-13 2x2g
gpu-node-14 3x0.5g (highly fragmented)
```

ben (eng-sre): preliminary hypothesis: mixed MIG profiles + long-lived low-priority slices = stranded fractional capacity. Autoscaler attempted scale-up but hit placement rules and cloud quota/backoff.

ryan (eng-platform): confirming autoscaler logs — scale-up requests were throttled due to quota and then retried with different MIG profile but backoff prevented timely retries. Cloud quota increase requested but ETA ~ 7-10m.

anya (customer-success): CS: two enterprise customers reporting degraded throughput and one opened a P1. Need ETA for mitigation to pass to them.

alice (eng-runtime): mitigation options: a) evict/terminate best-effort pods to defragment, b) relax strict binpack policy temporarily to allow spreading, c) spin up emergency full-GPU (no MIG) instances, d) route critical orgs to dedicated pre-warmed pool, e) apply model-fallbacks for non-SLA routes.

ben (eng-sre): safe rapid plan: cordon/drain most fragmented nodes, evict best-effort pods, relax binpack for 10m, and request emergency full-GPUs. I'll start with cordon/drain on worst offenders.

ben (eng-sre): executing:
```
kubectl label node gpu-node-14 temporary-maintenance=true
kubectl drain gpu-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30
```

deployer-bot: fallback route applied: /v1/chat -> fallback-cpu-small for non-SLA orgs at 2026-03-15T10:07:14Z

anya (customer-success): telling affected customers we applied temporary fallbacks and working on capacity. two customers accepted degraded latency fallback, one requested immediate escalation.

ryan (eng-platform): spinning 3 x full-gpu on-demand instances without MIG slicing to absorb burst while quota bump completes. Kube nodes are joining cluster now.

alice (eng-runtime): applied scheduler patch to relax binpack: `scheduler.binpack.enabled=false` for us-east-1. Also increased placement fragmentation tolerance to 0.25. Rolling now.

ben (eng-sre): drain+evict completed on 4 nodes, reclaimed ~7g contiguous capacity. queue reduced from ~1,280 -> ~430 in ~6 minutes.

alice (eng-runtime): autoscaler reconciled and accepted new nodes; backlog draining. Still seeing priority throttling on a few routes. Monitoring tail latencies and OOM/evictions.

ryan (eng-platform): quota bump approved; will replace emergency full-GPU instances with properly sliced MIG nodes when stable; planning to scale down emergency nodes in 15m.

ben (eng-sre): summary so far: root cause appears to be a confluence — mixed MIG profiles across fleet, long-lived low-priority slices preventing contiguous allocations, autoscaler conservative backoff + cloud quota friction. That resulted in stranded fractional GPU capacity and failed scale-up.

alice (eng-runtime): proposed post-incident actions:
- standardize allowed MIG profiles per region (reduce heterogeneity)
- autoscaler rule: when fragmentation > threshold, prefer full-GPU node creation to avoid failed binpack attempts
- implement proactive defragmenter to consolidate low-priority slices during low-traffic windows
- quota fallback paths to request alternate instance types when preferred profile unavailable

ben (eng-sre): short-term runbook items (assigned):
- ryan: confirm cloud quota adjustments + terminate emergency full-GPUs when stable
- alice: revert scheduler relaxation after stabilization and propose controlled rollout for policy change
- miguel: prepare customer incident summary + public status update
- ben: schedule repeated consolidation runs every 12h until defragmenter is deployed

miguel (oncall): handing incident lead to @ben for next 45m for remediation and follow-ups. I'll handle comms and postmortem kickoff.

ben (eng-sre): update: queue now ~35, GPU avg util down to ~68%. Throttling mostly cleared. Monitoring for 30m window.

anya (customer-success): will confirm with customers and close escalations after 1h stable. Thanks team.

deployer-bot: deployment 1a2b3c4 (scheduler policy change) completed in inference-runtime/us-east-1

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. incident_id=INC-20260315-1199

ben (eng-sre): creating PM ticket PM-3328 to track MIG standardization and defragmenter design. Marking thread resolved for now; reopen if regressions observed. :white_check_mark:
